§6Long-Lived Nuclear Waste§f

§aThe good stuff lives in the long-lived waste. Plutonium, bismuth, rare isotopes.§f

§bLong-Lived Nuclear Waste§f is a class of waste with long half-lives, derived from transuranic elements and neutron capture products. There are §e5 sub-classes§f: Th-232, U-233, U-235, Np-237, and Sa-326.

§6Non-Decayed Recycling§f:
§b•§f §bTh-232§f → §e40% U-233§f, §e35% U-235§f, §e25% waste
§b•§f §bU-233§f → §e15% U-235§f, §e25% Np-237§f, §e45% Pu-239§f, §e15% Tc-99§f
§b•§f §bU-235§f → §e25% Np-237§f, §e45% Pu-239§f, §e15% Pu-240§f, §e15% Tc-99§f
§b•§f §bNp-237§f → §e15% U-238§f, §e40% Pu-239§f, §e15% Pu-240§f, §e15% Tc-99§f, §e15% waste
§b•§f §bSa-326§f → §e25% Sa-327§f, §e18% Euphemium§f, §e16% Ghiorsium-336§f, §e8% Tantalium§f, §e8% Neodymium§f, §e25% waste

§6Decayed Yields§f (after §bNuclear Waste Disposal Drum§f):
§b•§f §bTh-232§f → Lead, Bismuth, Dust, waste
§b•§f §bU-233§f → mostly Lead
§b•§f §bNp-237§f → U-238, Lead, Dust, waste

§6Alternative§f: Feed it into a §bRadiation-Powered Engine§f to generate energy while it decays.

§ePS:§f Long-Lived Waste is §evaluable§f. It's loaded with Pu-239 and U-233 that recycle back into fuel. Don't dump it, process it.
